citation.title: Two-scale topology optimization of multiscale structures and materials via deep neural networks for local and global buckling
citation.authors: Sobhan Honarvar, Nolan Black, Ahmad R. Najafi
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering
citation.version_coded: Version of record metadata/abstract (full text inaccessible)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The DNN surrogate is presented as enabling higher-dimensional two-scale optimization that would be impractical with finite-element homogenization at every iteration.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The abstract gives a qualitative computational-cost comparison; it states no speed-up factor.
claim.alternatives: The abstract reports comparable global buckling performance for ellipse-based cells and less degradation when microscale buckling protection is active.

baseline.problem_size: Higher-dimensional microstructure design spaces (abstract; no dimensions given)
baseline.data_generation_cost: Finite-element homogenization data used for training; amount/cost not stated in abstract
baseline.quality_metric: Macro- and micro-scale buckling load factors (abstract)
baseline.quality_gap: Ellipse-based unit cells reported comparable global buckling performance to lattice cells (abstract)

notes: Abstract accessible from publisher and Drexel repository metadata. The repository identifies the version of record as open access under CC BY-NC 4.0 but links to the publisher DOI; the publisher PDF endpoint returned 403. No bot check was bypassed and no full text was obtained.
